Issachar
ISS-uh-kar
proper noun (figure / tribe)
Hebrew Yissaskar (H3485) — "there is reward" or "man of hire" (Gen 30:18); the ninth son of Jacob and the fifth of Leah; tribal patriarch of Issachar, settled in the fertile Jezreel Valley.

📖 Biblical Definition

Issachar is the fifth son of Leah (after Reuben, Simeon, Levi, and Judah, with Naphtali and the handmaids' children in between), born when Leah "hired" Jacob's company from Rachel by giving up some mandrakes (Gen 30:14-18). Leah named the boy with the cry "God hath given me my hire" (Gen 30:18) — the Hebrew sakar meaning "hire, wages, reward." The name carries some residue of the awkward mandrake-hire arrangement, but Leah received it as God's grace. Jacob's blessing on Issachar was startlingly mixed: "Issachar is a strong ass couching down between two burdens: And he saw that rest was good, and the land that it was pleasant; and bowed his shoulder to bear, and became a servant unto tribute" (Gen 49:14-15). The tribe got a fertile inheritance in the Jezreel Valley but tended toward settled comfort and tributary service rather than aggressive independence. Yet 1 Chronicles 12:32 gives the tribe's great moment of glory: "the children of Issachar, which were men that HAD UNDERSTANDING OF THE TIMES, to know what Israel ought to do" — the tribe that knew the season and the call. The Issacharites were Israel's calendar-readers, the tribe that knew when to act and when to wait. This is one of the great biblical descriptions of practical-prophetic discernment, and modern Christians often quote it ("sons of Issachar who understood the times") to describe leaders who can read cultural seasons and call God's people to right action. The tribe's land gave abundance; the tribe's discernment gave timing.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

Ninth son of Jacob, fifth of Leah; "there is reward" (Gen 30:18); the tribe of "understanding of the times" (1 Chr 12:32) — Israel's calendar-readers.

ISSACHAR, noun. (1) The ninth son of Jacob, fifth son of Leah (Gen 30:18). (2) The tribe descended from him, settled in the Jezreel Valley.

Hebrew Yissaskar — "there is reward" / "man of hire." Jacob's mixed blessing (Gen 49:14-15) and the great Chronicler's praise: "men that had understanding of the times, to know what Israel ought to do" (1 Chr 12:32).

📖 Key Scripture

Genesis 30:18 — "And Leah said, God hath given me my hire, because I have given my maiden to my husband: and she called his name Issachar."

Genesis 49:14-15 — "Issachar is a strong ass couching down between two burdens: And he saw that rest was good, and the land that it was pleasant; and bowed his shoulder to bear, and became a servant unto tribute."

1 Chronicles 12:32 — "And of the children of Issachar, which were men that had understanding of the times, to know what Israel ought to do; the heads of them were two hundred; and all their brethren were at their commandment."

Deuteronomy 33:18 — "And of Zebulun he said, Rejoice, Zebulun, in thy going out; and, Issachar, in thy tents."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

Issachar is corrupted when the modern "sons of Issachar who understood the times" cliché is severed from the canonical context (1 Chr 12 lists Issachar as one of many tribes who came to David at Hebron, not as a stand-alone discernment-of-cultural-trends formula), or when Jacob's mixed blessing is collapsed into either pure praise or pure rebuke.

expand to see more

"Understanding of the times" cliché. Modern American evangelical leadership culture has lifted 1 Chronicles 12:32 out of context and turned it into a slogan for cultural-trend-watching ministry, conferences, and political punditry. The canonical context is narrower: the Issacharites in 1 Chr 12 knew that David should be king at Hebron when other tribes were still waiting. Their discernment was COVENANT-DAVIDIC, not generic cultural intelligence. Christian leaders who claim the Issacharite mantle should be discerning what GOD WANTS HIS PEOPLE TO DO right now — not just what cultural trends might affect ministry.

Mixed-blessing collapse. Jacob's Genesis 49:14-15 word on Issachar is sometimes read as straight praise (settled, peaceful, content) and sometimes as straight rebuke (too comfortable, too tributary, too unwilling to fight for independence). The canonical text holds both: Issachar saw that rest was GOOD and the land was PLEASANT (real virtues), but bowed his shoulder to bear and became a servant unto tribute (real losses). The lesson: tribes / people / churches that prize comfort can lose strategic position. The Issacharite virtue (discernment of times) had to be COUPLED with willingness to ACT on the discernment, or the comfort-loving tendency would dominate.

Usage

"Issachar means THERE IS REWARD — Leah's cry at the birth that came through the awkward mandrake-hire."

"The children of Issachar had understanding of the times, to know what Israel ought to do — biblical pattern of practical discernment."
